newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia markets take Thai baht news in stride.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia markets take Thai baht news in stride.

text.p: Malaysian stocks were unmoved on Wednesday by the Thai baht's flotation as players took their cue from the stable ringgit, analysts said.
The Thai decision had been largely expected and was hailed as positive for regional markets despite the immediate sharp fall in the baht against the dollar, they said.
At about 0340 GMT, the key Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange's Composite Index was up 1.38 points at 1,080.28, continuing the lukewarm trading seen in recent weeks.
The focus remained on a clutch of speculative issues with big-capitalised stocks taking a back seat.
The ringgit slipped against the dollar in early morning trading but quickly recovered on the central Bank Negara's intervention, dealers said.

"I think the baht news was discounted. Hedge funds can only make money if people don't expect them to come in," said Phuah Lee Kerk, head of research at Jupiter Securities. "I think Bank Negara has sharpened its knife, waiting for them to come in," he added.
At about 0355 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.5229/34 to the dollar, up from its lowest level of 2.5250 in the morning when Bank Negara intervened.
Analysts said Malaysia was not being attacked by speculators as the Malaysian economy was on a firmer footing than Thailand's.

"Malaysian fundamentals are much more superior. It's stronger even when compared to Indonesia and the Philippines". "I don't think the float will spill over into the region," said Ng Bok Eng, regional economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.

Said Hugh Young, managing director at Aberdeen Asset Managers in Singapore: "In itself, it (the baht flotation) is not going to have any effect. But it does highlight the growing-up in general for the region."
